title: DeploymentOpsContract
purpose: Machine-readable deployment authority contract for Oyatie cloud cells: native release-conveyor and KRM/CUE desired state own deployment, Prow/Kubernetes-native oya-ci owns Buck2 evidence, and controller reconciliation owns day-2 convergence.
description: Deployment entrypoints are controller-owned, Kubernetes-native, and Buck2/Prow evidenced. Human-local commands are limited to static validation and PR evidence collection; provider-specific and third-party delivery tools are compatibility adapters only, never active deployment authority.

_meta.amendment_note: Reframes deployment authority around native release-conveyor, KRM/CUE desired state, Cluster API/Talos fleet controllers, and Buck2/Prow oya-ci evidence. Historical external IaC/app-delivery and local wrapper entrypoints are archive/provenance only.
source_directives: no handrolled mutable deployment paths; desired state is typed, reviewed, and controller-reconciled
after bootstrap, deployment and day-2 changes flow through native release-conveyor APIs, KRM/CUE desired-state packages, and controller reconciliation
no ad hoc host-login troubleshooting as the normal path; incident work records audit evidence and restores desired state through PR/controller reconciliation
cluster lifecycle uses Cluster API and Talos-compatible controllers; application rollout uses native release-conveyor progressive delivery

deployment_authority.rationale: The durable deployment source of truth is provider-neutral desired state plus signed build/evidence/release ledgers. Buck2/Prow produces immutable artifacts and evidence; the release-conveyor consumes that evidence and reconciles progressive delivery through Kubernetes-native controllers.
authority_boundaries: Prow/Kubernetes-native oya-ci owns trusted required-context publication
native release-conveyor owns promotion, rollback, and release-ledger state
KRM/CUE packages own first-party cloud-cell desired state and validation
provider-specific adapters are replaceable edges and must not become first-class deployment authority

roots.state_policy: signed release ledger plus progressive-delivery controller state
trusted controller-generated required context and ProwJob inventory
cluster lifecycle reconciled from reviewed KRM/CUE-generated desired state
immutable node configuration generated from reviewed desired-state inputs
cell boundary, service identity, and network-policy intent are controller reconciled
policy-as-code admission guardrails validate workload identity, privilege, and runtime posture

cluster_fleet.model: Cluster API + Talos-compatible node lifecycle + CUE/KRM desired state + native release-conveyor
cluster_fleet.node_install: immutable node bootstrap inputs generated from reviewed desired state; node lifecycle is reconciled by controllers rather than local operator scripts
cluster_fleet.cluster_lifecycle: Cluster API-compatible controllers reconcile cluster and cell resources from lane-owned desired-state shards
cluster_fleet.bootstrap_addons: controller-applied cell baseline includes networking, policy-as-code admission, workload identity, secrets integration, observability, and oya-ci runner isolation
cluster_fleet.app_delivery: native release-conveyor progressive delivery consumes signed Buck2/Prow artifacts and release-ledger approvals

operator_entrypoints.command_policy: Local commands may collect static evidence and open PRs only. Deployment mutation runs through native release-conveyor/controller APIs after trusted Buck2/Prow evidence is green. Local wrapper commands, provider adapter commands, and direct cluster mutation are not active deployment authority.

bootstrap_contract.entrypoint: native controller bootstrap through reviewed desired-state PR
bootstrap_contract.scope_note: Bootstrap establishes controller prerequisites and cell baseline desired state. It does not perform local imperative deployment; the release-conveyor and reconcilers converge state from reviewed inputs.
normal_flow: open a lane PR containing desired-state and release-conveyor inputs
run Buck2/Prow evidence and publish oya-ci-required from trusted controller state
release-conveyor records release ledger entry and starts progressive rollout
controllers reconcile cluster, workload, policy, identity, secrets, and observability resources
post rollout evidence, SLO, and audit rows before promotion
fleet_bring_up_separate: hardware or provider capacity is declared as desired state
Cluster API-compatible controllers reconcile control-plane and worker resources
cell registration and baseline policy are admitted only after Buck2/Prow evidence and policy-as-code checks pass
bootstrap_contract.confirmation_policy: Promotion requires trusted oya-ci-required evidence, release-ledger admission, scoped identity, and progressive-delivery health gates; hidden auto-approve paths are forbidden.

ops_management_contract.day_2_surface: native release-conveyor and cloud-cell controller APIs
ops_management_contract.rule: After bootstrap, desired-state changes, drift repair, status, and incident workflows are initiated through native APIs/controllers and PR-backed desired-state updates, not ad hoc host sessions or external substrate dashboards.
incident_flow: auto-rollback first when canary, SLO, or health gates fail
write registry/incidents/<id>.json evidence and dual-attribution audit rows
route code fixes through hotfix PRs with Buck2/Prow evidence
route infra/config/capacity fixes through desired-state PRs and controller reconciliation
restore declarative desired state before closing incident

break_glass.surface: controller-scoped emergency action with time-bound identity and audit evidence
preconditions: active production safety incident where native controllers or release-conveyor are unavailable
dual-attribution audit row emitted before or immediately after action
time-bound privilege escalation and session revocation are recorded
follow-up PR restores reviewed desired state
break_glass.expiration: emergency privilege expires automatically and cannot become a durable operating path

acceptance_criteria.rule: deployment mutation authority is native release-conveyor plus KRM/CUE desired state and controller reconciliation
Buck2/Prow oya-ci-required is the trusted merge and release evidence context
provider adapter, third-party delivery, local wrapper, and direct cluster mutation paths are adapter or break-glass only
incident remediation restores desired state through PR/controller reconciliation and records audit evidence
